heroSub: 11 hand-picked Ang Thong hotels across every budget — from a new town-centre hotel and a Japanese-style boutique to garden resorts by the river and a rice-field homestay near Wat Muang. Covering the town centre, the city edge and rural Chaiyo–Wiset Chai Chan. From roughly ฿300–950/night.
introH2: 🛕 Why does choosing the right area in Ang Thong matter so much?
introHtml: Ang Thong is a small province many people visit to pay respects at its famous temples — Wat Muang (home to the largest Buddha statue), Wat Pa Mok, Wat Chaiyo Worawihan — and to see the drum-making village of Ekarat. Stays fall into three sides with very different feels — central Ang Thong has hotels and boutiques near the market, the clock tower and the riverside Chao Phraya restaurants, ideal if you want easy access to food; the city edge and riverside has quiet single-storey garden resorts, good for self-drivers wanting peace; and rural Chaiyo–Wiset Chai Chan–Pho Thong has resorts and homestays in the rice fields near Wat Muang, ideal for temple-goers wanting rice-field views. Ang Thong is small — driving across takes no more than 20–40 minutes — but matching the area to your plan makes the trip easier. This guide rounds up 11 hand-picked Ang Thong hotels across every tier — all with real guest reviews, prices compared across 3 sites and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Ang Thong has no metro, no airport and no railway station — most people drive themselves or take a van or coach from Bangkok (about 1.5–2 hours) and then get around by car. Pick by your itinerary: the town centre (Talat Luang–Phosa–Ban It) is near the market, the riverside Chao Phraya restaurants and the town, best if you want easy access to food; the city edge and riverside (Sala Daeng–Pa Ngiu) has quiet garden resorts, good for self-drivers wanting peace; and rural Chaiyo–Wiset Chai Chan–Pho Thong is near Wat Muang, Wat Chaiyo and the drum-making village, ideal for temple-goers and a rice-field stay. Almost everywhere has free parking, so they suit self-drivers very well.

entries.name: Suphorn Grand Hotel
entries.revCount: 15 reviews · 9.3 · the highest in this guide · opened 2023
entries.badge: 🏆 Top score 9.3 · new build in town
entries.storyHtml: Suphorn Grand Hotel is a 2023 new-build with the highest review score in this guide — 9.3 (from 15 reviews). It's a fresh building in central Ang Thong, with clean rooms in new condition from Superior up to the larger Deluxe and Suite. From ฿900, the price suits the fresh rooms for a 3-star — a fit for anyone wanting a well-kept in-town hotel near the centre and restaurants.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If your budget stretches, take a Deluxe (King) — it's larger and more recently styled, much airier for only a few hundred baht more.

entries.name: IKKYU2 Ang Thong
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Bypass Rd · Phosa · Mueang Ang Thong
entries.addr: Bypass Rd, Phosa, Mueang Ang Thong
entries.storyHtml: IKKYU2 is a small Japanese-style boutique stay with a strong 9.0 from 29 reviews. Its draw is the minimalist Japanese decor: Standard King rooms with private balconies and a Netflix-ready TV, with a quiet, private feel since there are only a few rooms. From ฿650, it sits on the bypass road on the Phosa side, a short drive into town — a fit for couples or anyone wanting a stay with style at a friendly price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Rooms are limited and the score is good, so it fills fast on long weekends — booking ahead pays off, and busy-period rates rise noticeably.

entries.storyHtml: Bualuang Hotel is the in-town hotel with the most reviews in this guide — 33 — and a low starting price of just ฿500, scoring 7.7. It's a set of detached blocks in a garden, with spacious rooms of around 25 sqm ranging from a large-bed room up to a Family Room. It sits on Ayutthaya-Ang Thong Road on the Phosa side near the centre — a fit for travellers wanting a spacious in-town room at a friendly price, with solid review data behind it.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Travelling as a group or family? Take the Premier Family Room (around 35–40 sqm) — split between you, the per-person cost drops.

entries.name: Hor Nok Hook Resort Ang Thong
entries.storyHtml: Hor Nok Hook Resort is a small 15-room garden resort on the Chaiyo side, scoring 8.3 from 25 reviews. Its draw is a quiet, restful setting near the river, with rooms that have private garden-facing balconies, and it's pet-friendly (a small pet fee applies). From just ฿580, it's near Wat Chaiyo Worawihan — a fit for self-drivers wanting a quiet, budget-friendly garden stay where they can bring their dog or cat.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Bringing a pet? Mention it when booking, as there's a small pet fee and the pet-friendly rooms are limited.

faqTitle: FAQ — common traveller questions about Ang Thong hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in in Ang Thong?
faq.a: It depends on your plans and whether you have a car. The town centre (Talat Luang–Phosa–Ban It) is near the market, the riverside Chao Phraya restaurants and the town, best if you want easy access to food (Suphorn Grand, IKKYU2, Bualuang Hotel, Blue House). The city edge and riverside (Sala Daeng–Pa Ngiu) has quiet garden resorts, good with a car (Bualuang Boutique, Rimchon, Mor Mor, Ratchapruek DC). Rural Chaiyo–Wiset Chai Chan–Pho Thong is near Wat Muang and Wat Chaiyo, good for temple-goers and a rice-field stay (Hor Nok Hook, Jumbo Villa, Baan Thung Ratchawan).

faq.q: ❓ How much do Ang Thong hotels cost?
faq.a: Ang Thong is very affordable: homestays and budget stays start around ฿300–600 (Baan Thung Ratchawan, Bualuang Hotel, Hor Nok Hook, Jumbo Villa, Rimchon); boutiques and resorts in town or on the city edge are around ฿600–950 (IKKYU2, Blue House, Bualuang Boutique, Ratchapruek DC, Mor Mor); and a new-build town hotel starts around ฿900 (Suphorn Grand).

faq.q: ❓ Visiting Wat Muang — where should I stay?
faq.a: Wat Muang (home to the largest Buddha statue) is on the Wiset Chai Chan–Pho Thong side. The nearest, temple-friendly stays are Baan Thung Ratchawan Homestay ฿300, a rice-field homestay near Wat Muang, and Jumbo Villa Resort ฿600, garden rooms in rural Wiset Chai Chan. You can also stay in town and drive over, as it's about 20–30 minutes from the town centre to Wat Muang.

faq.q: ❓ Visiting Ang Thong without a car — where's convenient?
faq.a: Ang Thong has no railway station or metro, so without your own car it's best to stay in town where food and taxis are easier to find. Suphorn Grand Hotel, IKKYU2, Bualuang Hotel and Blue House are in town near the market and restaurants — walking or a short ride is more convenient than the rural stays.

faq.q: ❓ Are there quiet garden stays in Ang Thong?
faq.a: Several. Hor Nok Hook Resort ฿580 is a pet-friendly garden resort in Chaiyo District; Bualuang Boutique Resort ฿600 has single-storey garden rooms on the city edge; Mor Mor Resort ฿950 is garden bungalows with rice-field views; and Jumbo Villa ฿600 has garden rooms with free bikes. All have a quiet feel and suit self-drivers.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book an Ang Thong hotel?
faq.a: On ordinary weekdays, booking 1–2 weeks ahead is plenty, as Ang Thong isn't a crowded market. But on long weekends and temple-visit holidays, small-room stays like IKKYU2 and little garden resorts like Hor Nok Hook fill fast, so book 2–3 weeks ahead or more.
